title: 'It started with a cup of tea - now we help thousands'

input.lead: Twenty-five years ago Victoria "put a kettle on" for her community.
input.summary: Twenty-five years ago Victoria "put a kettle on" for her community. Now she helps more than 2,000 people
input.evidence_text: When Victoria Armstrong moved to Manchester as a university student in the 1990s she started to notice there were people living in her community who "had no-one" "I spent the first six months just putting on a kettle and putting bread in the toaster," the 53-year-old said Victoria, originally from Oxford, who had moved to Gorton after enrolling as a Fine Art student at Manchester University, started to host people for a cup of tea at her local church once a week Later she made it an official charity, founding Oasis in 2001 "It started with cups of tea and toast," Victoria said. "Twenty-five years later and we have helped thousands of people." Oasis now has its own centre, with 19 staff and 90 volunteers, running education classes, a free cafe, crisis support services, job clubs and a charity shop

title: Train station returning to Cheadle after more than 100 years

input.lead: Cheadle in Stockport has been without a train station since its original hub closed in 1917
input.summary: Cheadle in Stockport has been without a train station since its original hub closed in 1917
input.evidence_text: Work is beginning on bringing a train station back to the heart of a Greater Manchester village more than a century after its original station closed Cheadle in Stockport had a station just off the high street up until 1917 Funding for a new hub, which would be built next to Alexandra Hospital, was given the green light in 2022, with planning permission granted in 2023 but concerns about its effect on the timetabling of trains elsewhere on the network led to delays Stockport Council said the issue had now been resolved and council leader Mark Roberts said it was "a hugely significant moment for Cheadle and for Stockport" "For years we've fought for this station because we know the difference it will make to residents, businesses and the future prosperity of the area," he added Roberts said he was delighted that the initial highways work could now start on site thanks to the persistence and partnership of all involved

title: Sir Kevin Sinfield completes epic challenge ahead of Grand Final

input.lead: Sir Kevin Sinfield crosses the finish line at Old Trafford after seven ultramarathons in seven days
input.summary: Sir Kevin Sinfield crosses the finish line at Old Trafford after seven ultramarathons in seven days
input.evidence_text: Sir Kevin Sinfield completes epic challenge ahead of Grand Final - BBC News Image source, Richard Sellers/PA Image caption, Kevin Sinfield carried the Super League Grand Final trophy into Old Trafford after completing the challenge By Grace Wood Yorkshire Published 3 October 2026 Updated 4 October 2026 Sir Kevin Sinfield has completed his latest endurance challenge raising money for motor neurone disease (MND) causes in memory of his friend and teammate Rob Burrow, who died in 2024. Sinfield completed seven ultramarathons in seven days, crossing the finish line at Old Trafford Stadium in Manchester ahead of the Super League Grand Final. The fundraiser and his team have raised more than £13m for the MND community since his first annual challenge in 2020. Speaking to the crowd, Sinfield said: "The rugby league community has got right behind the MND community and Rob would be so proud to see how you've supported and cared, and showed your love for a community that really needs us." Sinfield began his final ultramarathon challenge in Hull on September 27 and visited all 12 UK Super League clubs along the way. The 7 in 7: The Grand Finale week ended at Old Trafford earlier where he brought out the trophy ahead of the game between Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity. The number of items found was confirmed to be between 10,000 and 11,000 It's understood that the worker involved, who is believed to have been employed by Royal Mail in Bury for a number of years, is no longer with the business. Royal Mail has not confirmed whether the matter has been referred to police for a criminal investigation The M.E.N. understands each item of mail currently being held by Royal Mail will be delivered to its rightful recipient, along with a covering letter explaining the circumstances. Since being handed over to Royal Mail by police, the mail has been kept at the Bury delivery office, It has since been sorted by delivery area and is now being prepared for delivery, it is understood. title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

input.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
input.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
input.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
